purpose: Category quotas for the seeded change corpus, fixed before any patch was authored. The ground-truth label of every patch is bce's verdict (labels.json), not the intent recorded here.

families.description: a file in src/domain imports from src/app or src/config (value or type import)
infrastructure reaches the core: src/domain imports src/infra or the pg package, or src/app imports the pg package or a file inside a src/infra subfolder
src/config reads an environment variable outside the allowlist (dotted or bracket access), or src/domain, src/app or src/infra reads process.env
a governed file re-exports a forbidden module (export { x } from, export * from, export type from)
a governed file loads a forbidden module with import(), with a string-literal or a computed specifier
a legal feature: new domain logic, a new use case through ports, a new repository method or route in infra, a new allowlisted setting use
a behaviour-preserving refactor: rename a symbol or file, extract a helper, reorder imports

an import that looks like a breach but is allowed: app through src/infra/index.ts, infra importing app or domain, the composition root importing infra internals, pg inside src/infra/db, an allowlisted process.env read in src/config
a change only under test/ (outside src/), which may import infra internals or read process.env
a comment in a .ts file, or a Markdown doc, that names a forbidden module or package without importing it

nearMissMinimum: at least one third of the clean items (>= 10 of 30); this spec plans 16
ruleCoverage: every blueprint constraint is the intended target of at least 2 drift items

removedFamilies.reason: WO-02 T-4 probe: a domain file importing an ungoverned barrel that re-exports infra is GREEN in bce 0.3.1 (direct import edges only), so bce cannot label it. Removed before authoring. The plain-language rules do not forbid it either.

ids.scheme: c001..c060, neutral; the patch file name carries no family or label
ids.assignment: a seeded shuffle of the authored items (seed recorded in manifest.json), so id order does not follow family order

sizeCap.measure: pre-cut Laya encoding of the full gate input: state = rules.txt + "\n\n" + diff, question and options included (laya_count.py)
sizeCap.rule: len(ids(state)) <= room (989 with this question); a patch over the room is re-authored smaller, never cut

amendments.trigger: WO-07 independent review, round 1 (FIX-NEEDED, finding F1): a keyword grep scored 0.92 with 0 missed RED items, because every RED item carried a rule keyword on an added code line and almost no GREEN item did.
amendments.note: Quotas, split, near-miss count and family names are unchanged. The family descriptions above are the originals and stay as committed; the lines below widen what each family may contain, so that GREEN items can use rule keywords in allowed places and RED items can break a rule without an import or code keyword.

descriptionAdds.forbidden-config-key: also: a comment in src/domain, src/app or src/infra that contains process.env, or a comment in src/config that names process.env.NAME outside the allowlist (bce's forbiddenPattern rules match comments; rules.txt lines 7 and 8 say so)
descriptionAdds.infra-leak: also: the pg package imported with double quotes
descriptionAdds.feature-add: also: a new file in a folder under src/ outside the four layers (for example src/jobs) that imports src/config and src/infra internals, and a new src/config file that reads an allowlisted variable
descriptionAdds.refactor-rename: also: a change of import style for the pg package inside src/infra
descriptionAdds.allowed-import-near-forbidden: also: src/app importing src/config or '../infra/index', a new src/infra/db file that imports pg, and the composition root loading an infra internal with import()
descriptionAdds.comment-or-doc-mention: also: a trailing comment on a code line that names a forbidden module path or the pg package

amendments.trigger: WO-07 independent review, round 1, finding F5: rules.txt lines 7 and 8 were reworded to state exactly what bce enforces.
amendments.note: sizeCap.rulesTokens above records rules.txt as it was when the cap was fixed (235 tokens). The reworded rules.txt measures 256 tokens with the same tokenizer (laya_count.py). The cap rule itself is unchanged: every state must fit the room of 989 tokens, and all 60 do (largest 923).
